title: 82% Of Americans Fly Once A Year Or Less—And Don’t Know The Rules
summary: Last Thanksgiving, if you saw an open aisle seat on Southwest Airlines, you were welcome to take it. Do exactly what you learned a year ago and this Thanksgiving you’re the guy holding up the aisle because the passenger behind you has a boarding pass for your seat, and you’re getting scolded by a flight attendant. You may not even know you were going to get charged for bags!

title: At One Chinese Airport, Passengers Aren’t Allowed To Look Out The Window [Roundup]
summary: Passengers had to close their window shades for landing at China’s Yanji Airport. One traveler says they then spent nearly 30 minutes circling with the shades down because military aircraft had priority. Plus, a cat gets loose midflight, and Phoenix’s new airport lounge will have a terrace overlooking Camelback Mountain.

title: FedEx Jet Runs Off Miami Runway 80 Days After Amazon Air Crash Killed 5 There
summary: FedEx flight 910 from Memphis ran off the end of runway 26R at Miami airport Wednesday night and stopped in the grass just inside the fence at NW 67th Avenue. From across the street, the nose of the MD-11 lined up with the traffic light. Both people aboard got out safely. Nobody on the ground was hurt.

title: Park Hyatt Beaver Creek Offers Up To 90,000 Points Back Over Christmas And New Year’s—If You Email The Hotel
summary: This amounts to a 27% discount against 55,000 point per night pricing, though this hotel can get even more expensive (e.g. December 22 at 65,000 points). And rooms run around $1,000 per night leading up to Christmas around around $2,000 between Christmas and New Year's. 40,000 points against peak rates works out nicely.

title: TSA Demanded United Airlines Suspend A Pilot Over Terror Support, Union Accused Of Resisting, Report Says
summary: TSA reportedly told United Airlines to suspend a pilot accused of supporting a terrorist group, after the pilots union resisted action according to a federal government source cited by TV news reporter Mike Wagenheim.

title: Warning For Families Traveling To California: New Booster Seat Law Covers Kids Through Age 15
summary: I have a California trip coming up with my family. If I hadn’t seen this on Twitter, it wouldn’t have occurred to me that my 8-year-old daughter might need a booster for the ride from the airport. They insist on measuring how the belt fits her in the car we actually wind up with from National, Avis or Uber.
